components.name: ECDSA secp256k1 (ethers v5 Wallet burner signer)

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hash.js (SHA-1/SHA-2 + ripemd160) is the hash layer of ethers v5: @ethersproject/signing-key/elliptic use its SHA-256/SHA-512 inside secp256k1 ECDSA and BIP-32 HMAC derivation, and @ethersproject/sha2 wraps it for keystore MACs. The D rating reflects SHA-1 being part of its surface; the Ethereum paths use SHA-256/SHA-512. Two sites = the lockfile declaration/resolution blocks for the package.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Pulled solely by mocha-junit-reporter@2.0.2 (yarn.lock:17582-17591) to fingerprint test cases in JUnit XML output — collision-broken MD5 used as a non-security identifier in the dev/test pipeline only. No application/product call site; the implementation still ships with the build. LIB-95605640 marked as the same logical dependency.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: secp256k1 ECDSA — the Ethereum signing primitive (every transaction/message signature). Three providers ship in the build: elliptic@6.5.4 via @ethersproject/signing-key@5.6.2 (direct dep of eth-hooks, live consumer useBurnerSigner.ts via ethers.Wallet); @noble/secp256k1@1.6.3 via @scure/bip32@1.1.0/@scure/bip39@1.1.0 (HD-wallet/mnemonic stack parallel to ethers, no app call site); and the browserify create-ecdh polyfill. The lockfile also carries legacy ethers@4.0.49 pinning the same elliptic 6.

components.name: Node.js tls sessions on default settings (at least Node.js 14)

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: PBKDF2 reaches the build via @ethersproject/pbkdf2 (BIP-39 mnemonic→seed: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512, 2048 iterations, protocol constant) and backs @ethersproject/json-wallets keystore encryption (Web3 Secret Storage v3, 262144-iteration pbkdf2 variant). Also present via crypto-browserify ^3.0.3 as the webpack crypto polyfill. Live path: ethers.Wallet.createRandom() in useBurnerSigner.ts derives through BIP-39 PBKDF2.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/hashes@1.1.2 enters the build via @scure/bip32@1.1.0 / @scure/bip39@1.1.0 (HD-wallet and BIP-39 mnemonic libraries, yarn.lock:3426-3430); SHA-256/SHA-512 feed the HMAC-based BIP-32/39 derivation there. Available in the shipped library; no application call site found — the app's own hashing goes through ethers (Keccak-256/SHA-2 via other packages).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: BLAKE3 ships inside @noble/hashes@1.1.2, pulled via @scure/bip32/bip39. No application or scure call site reaches BLAKE3 specifically, but the implementation ships with the build. Quantum-safe hash (Grover only halves preimage resistance).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-3 ships inside @noble/hashes@1.1.2 (pulled via @scure/bip32/bip39). Note this is noble's FIPS-202 SHA3: it is NOT Ethereum's Keccak-256 (pre-FIPS padding), which arrives separately via @ethersproject/keccak256@5.6.1 → js-sha3@0.8.0 and is reported as its own finding.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt memory-hard KDF in two resolutions: scrypt-js@3.0.1 backs ethers v5 keystore encryption (@ethersproject/json-wallets@5.6.1, Web3 Secret Storage v3, scrypt N=131072) and scrypt-js@2.0.4 is pinned by the legacy ethers@4.0.49 also present in the lockfile (yarn.lock:12227-12239). Used whenever a keystore JSON is created/unlocked; the app's burner key path stores the key unencrypted instead (see useBurnerSigner finding).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Consumed by create-hash@1.2.0 (sha.js ^2.4.0) and create-hmac@1.1.7 (sha.js ^2.4.8) — the browserify crypto polyfill webpack injects for require('crypto') in the docs/build toolchain (yarn.lock:8541-8561). No application call site; the SHA-1/SHA-2 capability ships with the build regardless.
